168class LexisResource:
169    """Information about LEXIS Resource entity and the quantum clusters assigned to it.
170
171    Attributes:
172        resource_name (str): The name of the resource.
173        project_resource_id (str): The ID of the resource assignment in LEXIS.
174        resource_validity_start (str): The start date of the resource validity.
175        resource_validity_end (str): The end date of the resource validity.
176        clusters (dict[str, QCluster]): A dictionary of clusters assigned to the resource.
177    """
178
179    def __init__(
180        self,
181        resource_name: str,
182        project_resource_id: str,
183        resource_validity_start: str,
184        resource_validity_end: str,
185        clusters: dict[str, QCluster] | None = None,
186    ):
187        """Initialize a new LexisResource instance.
188
189        Args:
190            resource_name (str): The name of the resource.
191            project_resource_id (str): The ID of the resource assignment in LEXIS.
192            resource_validity_start (str): The start date of the resource validity.
193            resource_validity_end (str): The end date of the resource validity.
194            clusters (dict[str, QCluster] | None, optional): A dictionary of clusters assigned to the resource. Defaults to None.
195        """
196        self._resource_name = resource_name
197        self._project_resource_id = project_resource_id
198        self._resource_validity_start = resource_validity_start
199        self._resource_validity_end = resource_validity_end
200        self._clusters: dict[str, QCluster] = dict(clusters or {})
201
202    @property
203    def resource_name(self) -> str:
204        """Get the name of the resource.
205
206        Returns:
207            str: The name of the resource.
208        """
209        return self._resource_name
210
211    @property
212    def project_resource_id(self) -> str:
213        """Get the ID of the resource assignment in LEXIS.
214
215        Returns:
216            str: The ID of the resource assignment in LEXIS.
217        """
218        return self._project_resource_id
219
220    @property
221    def resource_validity_start(self) -> str:
222        """Get the start date of the resource validity.
223
224        Returns:
225            str: The start date of the resource validity.
226        """
227        return self._resource_validity_start
228
229    @property
230    def resource_validity_end(self) -> str:
231        """Get the end date of the resource validity.
232
233        Returns:
234            str: The end date of the resource validity.
235        """
236        return self._resource_validity_end
237
238    @property
239    def clusters(self) -> dict[str, QCluster]:
240        """Get the clusters assigned to the resource.
241
242        Returns:
243            dict[str, QCluster]: A dictionary of clusters assigned to the resource.
244        """
245        return self._clusters
246
247    @property
248    def cluster_names(self) -> list[str]:
249        """Get the names of the clusters assigned to the resource.
250
251        Returns:
252            list[str]: A list of cluster names.
253        """
254        return sorted(self._clusters)
255
256    @property
257    def allocated_units(self) -> int:
258        """Get the sum of allocations over all clusters of the resource.
259
260        Returns:
261            int: The sum of allocations.
262        """
263        return sum(c.allocated_units or 0 for c in self._clusters.values())
264
265    def get_cluster(self, name: str) -> QCluster:
266        """Get a specific cluster by name.
267
268        Args:
269            name (str): The name of the cluster.
270
271        Returns:
272            QCluster: The cluster with the specified name.
273
274        Raises:
275            KeyError: If the cluster is not found.
276        """
277        try:
278            return self._clusters[name]
279        except KeyError:
280            raise KeyError(
281                f"Cluster '{name}' not found in resource '{self._resource_name}'. "
282                f"Available: {self.cluster_names}"
283            ) from None

class QBackend(qiskit.providers.backend.BackendV2, abc.ABC): 
 49class QBackend(BackendV2, ABC):
 50    """Abstract QaaS backend backed by QClient. Subclasses must implement run() returning QJob.
 51
 52    Deliberately does not define `target` or `max_circuits`, so a vendor base class
 53    placed after it in the MRO (e.g. IQMBackendBase) can supply them.
 54    """
 55
 56    def __init__(self, client: QClient, **kwargs):
 57        """Initialize the QBackend with a QClient.
 58
 59        Args:
 60            client (QClient): The QClient instance to use for communication with the backend.
 61            **kwargs: Additional keyword arguments to be passed to the BackendV2 constructor.
 62        """
 63        # Cooperative init: forwards remaining kwargs along the MRO (vendor base -> BackendV2).
 64        # TODO: finish readable kwargs for BackendV2 from QISKIT, e.g. provider, name, description, version, url, etc.
 65        BackendV2.__init__(self)
 66        self._qclient = client
 67
 68    @classmethod
 69    def _default_options(cls) -> Options:
 70        """Return the default options for the backend.
 71
 72        Returns:
 73            Options: The default options: ``shots=1024`` and ``memory=False``.
 74        """
 75        return Options(shots=1024, memory=False)
 76
 77    @abstractmethod
 78    def run(
 79        self,
 80        run_input: QuantumCircuit | list[QuantumCircuit],
 81        shots: int | None = None,
 82        **options,
 83    ) -> "QJob":
 84        """Serialize circuit(s) and submit them; must return a QJob.
 85
 86        Args:
 87            run_input (QuantumCircuit | list[QuantumCircuit]): The quantum circuit(s) to run.
 88            shots (int | None): The number of shots to execute; the backend's ``shots``
 89                option (``backend.options.shots``) if ``None``, as ``BackendV2.run()`` expects.
 90            **options: Additional options for the run.
 91
 92        Returns:
 93            QJob: The QJob instance representing the submitted job.
 94        """
 95
 96    @abstractmethod
 97    def result_to_qiskit(
 98        self,
 99        raw: list[dict],
100        measurements_raw: list[dict] | None = None,
101        reg_name: str = "meas",
102    ) -> PrimitiveResult:
103        """Convert raw results and measurements to a Qiskit PrimitiveResult.
104
105        Args:
106            raw (list[dict]): List of dictionaries containing raw results from the quantum backend.
107            measurements_raw (list[dict] | None): Optional list of dictionaries containing raw measurements.
108            reg_name (str): Name of the register to use for measurements.
109
110        Returns:
111            PrimitiveResult: A Qiskit PrimitiveResult object.
112        """
113
114    @abstractmethod
115    def result_to_qiskit_legacy(
116        self,
117        raw: list[dict],
118        measurements_raw: list[dict] | None = None,
119        reg_name: str = "meas",
120        backend_name: str = "my_backend",
121        job_id: str = "",
122        circuit_headers: list[dict[str, Any]] | None = None,
123    ) -> Result:
124        """Convert raw results to a Qiskit Result object in legacy format.
125
126        Args:
127            raw (list[dict]): A list of dictionaries containing measurement keys and counts.
128                Each dictionary should have the form:
129                {"measurement_keys": [...], "counts": {...}}
130            measurements_raw (list[dict] | None): Optional, one dictionary per PUB containing raw measurements.
131                If provided, used instead of counts to preserve shot order.
132                Format: {key: [[bit, ...], ...shots]}
133            reg_name (str): The name of the classical register to use for measurement results.
134            backend_name (str): The name of the backend used for the execution.
135            job_id (str): The ID of the job that produced the results.
136            circuit_headers (list[dict[str, Any]] | None): Optional, one
137                ``{"name": ..., "metadata": ...}`` per circuit for the experiment headers.
138
139        Returns:
140            Result: A Result object containing the processed measurement results.
141
142        Raises:
143            ValueError: If the number of raw results does not match the number of measurement sets.
144        """
145
146    def _submit(
147        self,
148        circuit_payloads: dict[str, str],
149        shots: int,
150        circuit_headers: list[dict[str, Any]] | None = None,
151        **options,
152    ) -> "QJob":
153        """Builds HEAppE tasks from {part_name: payload} and submits them via QClient.
154
155        Args:
156            circuit_payloads (dict[str, str]): A dictionary mapping part names to circuit payloads.
157            shots (int): The number of shots to execute.
158            circuit_headers (list[dict[str, Any]] | None): ``{"name", "metadata"}`` of each
159                submitted circuit, put into the result headers.
160            **options: Additional options for the submission, such as walltime_limit_secs, use_sessions
161                and memory (if True, the job's results include per-shot measurements by default).
162
163        Returns:
164            QJob: The QJob instance representing the submitted job.
165        """
166        machine_id = self._qclient.get_quantum_backend_info().backend_name
167
168        tasks = [
169            {
170                "Name": f"qheappe_task_{i}",
171                "MachineId": machine_id,
172                "WalltimeLimitSecs": options.get("walltime_limit_secs", 3600),
173                "PayloadPartName": part_name,
174                "UseSessions": options.get("use_sessions", False),
175                "EnvironmentVariables": {"RUN_SHOTS": str(shots)},
176            }
177            for i, part_name in enumerate(circuit_payloads)
178        ]
179
180        submitted_job = self._qclient._run(
181            self._qclient.submit_quantum_job(
182                tasks=tasks,
183                job_name=options.get("job_name", "qiskit_qasm_job"),
184                circuit_payloads=circuit_payloads,
185            )
186        )
187        heappe_job_id = (
188            submitted_job.get("Id")
189            if isinstance(submitted_job, dict)
190            else submitted_job
191        )
192
193        return QJob(
194            backend=self,
195            heappe_job_id=heappe_job_id,
196            submitted_job=submitted_job,
197            shots=shots,
198            memory=bool(options.get("memory", self.options.memory)),
199            circuit_headers=circuit_headers,
200        )
201
202    @abstractmethod
203    def transpile(
204        self, circuits: list[QuantumCircuit] | QuantumCircuit, **kwargs
205    ) -> list[QuantumCircuit] | QuantumCircuit:
206        """Transpile circuits to target machine.
207
208        Args:
209            circuits (list[QuantumCircuit] | QuantumCircuit): The quantum circuit(s) to transpile.
210            **kwargs: Additional keyword arguments for the transpiler.
211
212        Returns:
213            list[QuantumCircuit] | QuantumCircuit: The transpiled quantum circuit(s).
214        """

Abstract QaaS backend backed by QClient. Subclasses must implement run() returning QJob.

Deliberately does not define target or max_circuits, so a vendor base class placed after it in the MRO (e.g. IQMBackendBase) can supply them.

Raises: ValueError: If the number of raw results does not match the number of measurement sets.

157class QBackendIQM(QBackend, IQMBackend):

159    execution goes through QClient/HEAppE.
160
161    Works with every supported IQM stack. Stack-specific subclasses
162    (``QBackendIQM35``, ``QBackendIQM36``) set :attr:`iqm_stack` and override
163    the hooks below where the IQM libraries differ.
164    """

171        """Build an ObservationFinder from a ``MachineCalibration`` metrics response.
172
173        Args:
174            metrics: Parsed metrics JSON with an ``observations`` list.
175
176        Returns:

238
239    def result_to_qiskit(
240        self,
241        raw: list[dict],
242        measurements_raw: list[dict] | None = None,
243        reg_name: str = "meas",
244    ) -> PrimitiveResult:
245        """
246        Convert raw results to a Qiskit PrimitiveResult object.
247
248        Args:
249            raw: A list of dictionaries containing measurement keys and counts.
250                 Each dictionary should have the form:
251                 {"measurement_keys": [...], "counts": {...}}
252            measurements_raw: Optional, one dictionary per PUB containing raw measurements.
253                              If provided, used instead of counts to preserve shot order.
254                              Format: {key: [[bit, ...], ...shots]}
255            reg_name: The name of the classical register to use for measurement results.
256
257        Bitstrings follow the Qiskit order (registers in circuit order, clbit 0
258        rightmost), using the IQM measurement keys. Results with other keys are
259        read as given, most significant bit first.
260
261        Returns:
262            A PrimitiveResult object containing the processed measurement results.
263        Raises:
264            ValueError: If the number of raw results does not match the number of measurement sets.
265            ValueError: If the shot counts differ between keys in a PUB.
266            ValueError: If the number of shots in measurements does not match the sum of counts.
267        """
268        if measurements_raw is not None and len(measurements_raw) != len(raw):
269            raise ValueError(
270                f"{len(raw)} results but {len(measurements_raw)} measurement sets"
271            )
272
273        pubs = []
274        for i, item in enumerate(raw):
275            keys = item["measurement_keys"]
276            item, m = _to_qiskit_order(
277                item, measurements_raw[i] if measurements_raw is not None else None
278            )
279            read_keys = item["measurement_keys"]
280
281            if m is not None:
282                cols = [
283                    np.asarray(m[k], dtype=bool).reshape(len(m[k]), -1)
284                    for k in read_keys
285                ]
286                if len({c.shape[0] for c in cols}) != 1:
287                    raise ValueError(f"PUB {i}: keys have different shot counts")
288                bitarray = BitArray.from_bool_array(
289                    np.concatenate(cols, axis=1), order="big"
290                )
291
292                if "counts" in item and bitarray.num_shots != sum(
293                    item["counts"].values()
294                ):
295                    raise ValueError(f"PUB {i}: shots in measurements != sum of counts")
296            else:
297                n = len(next(iter(item["counts"])))
298                int_counts = {int(bs, 2): c for bs, c in item["counts"].items()}
299                bitarray = BitArray.from_counts(int_counts, num_bits=n)
300
301            data = DataBin(**{reg_name: bitarray}, shape=bitarray.shape)
302            pubs.append(SamplerPubResult(data, metadata={"measurement_keys": keys}))
303        return PrimitiveResult(pubs, metadata={})
304
305    def result_to_qiskit_legacy(
306        self,
307        raw: list[dict],
308        measurements_raw: list[dict] | None = None,
309        reg_name: str = "meas",
310        backend_name: str = "my_backend",
311        job_id: str = "",
312        circuit_headers: list[dict[str, Any]] | None = None,
313    ) -> Result:
314        """
315        Convert raw results to a Qiskit Result object in legacy format.
316
317        Args:
318            raw: A list of dictionaries containing measurement keys and counts.
319                 Each dictionary should have the form:
320                 {"measurement_keys": [...], "counts": {...}}
321            measurements: Optional, one dictionary per PUB containing raw measurements.
322                          If provided, used instead of counts to preserve shot order.
323                          Format: {key: [[bit, ...], ...shots]}
324            reg_name: The name of the classical register to use for measurement results.
325            backend_name: The name of the backend used for the execution.
326            job_id: The ID of the job that produced the results.
327            circuit_headers: Optional, one ``{"name": ..., "metadata": ...}`` per circuit,
328                copied into each experiment's header (so ``get_counts(circuit)`` works).
329                Experiments are named ``circuit-<i>`` without it.
330
331        Bitstrings follow the Qiskit order (registers in circuit order, clbit 0
332        rightmost), using the IQM measurement keys. The IQM keys also give the
333        classical registers, so counts read e.g. ``"0 01"`` for registers ``a`` (2 bits)
334        and ``b`` (1 bit), as in Qiskit. Results with other keys are read as given,
335        most significant bit first, as one register ``reg_name``.
336
337        Returns:
338            A Result object containing the processed measurement results.
339
340        Raises:
341            ValueError: If the number of raw results does not match the number of measurement sets.
342        """
343
344        if circuit_headers is not None and len(circuit_headers) != len(raw):
345            circuit_headers = None  # e.g. a job re-created with different circuits
346
347        exps = []
348        for i, item in enumerate(raw):
349            keys = item["measurement_keys"]
350            creg_sizes = _iqm_creg_sizes(keys)
351            info = circuit_headers[i] if circuit_headers else {}
352            item, m = _to_qiskit_order(
353                item, measurements_raw[i] if measurements_raw is not None else None
354            )
355            counts = {hex(int(bs, 2)): c for bs, c in item["counts"].items()}
356            n = len(next(iter(item["counts"])))
357
358            memory = None
359            if m is not None:
360                per_key = [m[k] for k in item["measurement_keys"]]  # [key][shot][bit]
361                shots = len(per_key[0])
362                bitstrs = [
363                    "".join(str(int(b)) for k in per_key for b in k[s])
364                    for s in range(shots)
365                ]
366                memory = [hex(int(s, 2)) for s in bitstrs]
367
368            exps.append(
369                ExperimentResult(
370                    shots=sum(item["counts"].values()),
371                    success=True,
372                    data=ExperimentResultData(counts=counts, memory=memory),
373                    header={
374                        "name": info.get("name") or f"circuit-{i}",
375                        "creg_sizes": creg_sizes or [[reg_name, n]],
376                        "memory_slots": n,
377                        "metadata": info.get("metadata") or {},
378                        "measurement_keys": keys,
379                    },
380                )
381            )
382
383        return Result(
384            backend_name=backend_name,
385            backend_version="1.0",
386            job_id=job_id,
387            success=True,
388            results=exps,
389        )
390
391    def create_run_request(
392        self,
393        run_input: QuantumCircuit | list[QuantumCircuit],
394        shots: int = 1024,
395        circuit_compilation_options: CircuitCompilationOptions | None = None,
396        circuit_callback: Callable[[list[QuantumCircuit]], Any] | None = None,
397        qubit_index_to_name: dict[int, str] | None = None,
398        **unknown_options,
399    ) -> CircuitJobDefinition:
400        """Alias of :meth:`create_circuit_job_definition` (iqm-client 35.x name)."""
401        return self.create_circuit_job_definition(
402            run_input,
403            shots=shots,
404            circuit_compilation_options=circuit_compilation_options,
405            circuit_callback=circuit_callback,
406            qubit_index_to_name=qubit_index_to_name,
407            **unknown_options,
408        )
409
410    def create_circuit_job_definition(
411        self,
412        run_input: QuantumCircuit | list[QuantumCircuit],
413        shots: int = 1024,
414        circuit_compilation_options: CircuitCompilationOptions | None = None,
415        circuit_callback: Callable[[list[QuantumCircuit]], Any] | None = None,
416        qubit_index_to_name: dict[int, str] | None = None,
417        **unknown_options,
418    ) -> CircuitJobDefinition:
419        """Create a circuit job definition (run request) without submitting it for execution.
420
421        This can be used to check what would be submitted for execution by an equivalent call to :meth:`run`.
422
423        Args:
424            run_input: Same as in :meth:`run`.
425
426        Args:
427            shots: Number of repetitions of each circuit, for sampling.
428            circuit_compilation_options:
429                Compilation options for the circuits, passed on to :class:`~iqm.iqm_client.iqm_client.IQMClient`.
430                If ``None``, the defaults of the :class:`~iqm.iqm_client.models.CircuitCompilationOptions`
431                class are used.
432            circuit_callback:
433                Callback function that, if provided, will be called for the circuits before sending
434                them to the device.  This may be useful in situations when you do not have explicit
435                control over transpilation, but need some information on how it was done. This can
436                happen, for example, when you use pre-implemented algorithms and experiments in
437                Qiskit, where the implementation of the said algorithm or experiment takes care of
438                delivering correctly transpiled circuits to the backend. This callback method gives
439                you a chance to look into those transpiled circuits, and extract any info you need.
440                As a side effect, you can also use this callback to modify the transpiled circuits
441                in-place, just before execution; however, we do not recommend to use it for this
442                purpose.
443            qubit_index_to_name: Mapping from qubit indices in the circuit to qubit names on the device.
444                If ``None``, :attr:`.IQMBackendBase.index_to_qubit_name` will be used.
445            unknown_options: Backwards compatibility for deprecated parameters.
446
447        Returns:
448            The created circuit job definition.
449
450        """
451        circuits = [run_input] if isinstance(run_input, QuantumCircuit) else run_input
452
453        if len(circuits) == 0:
454            raise ValueError("Empty list of circuits submitted for execution.")
455
456        # Catch old iqm-client options
457        if (
458            "max_circuit_duration_over_t2" in unknown_options
459            or "heralding_mode" in unknown_options
460        ):
461            warnings.warn(
462                DeprecationWarning(
463                    "max_circuit_duration_over_t2 and heralding_mode are deprecated, please use "
464                    + "circuit_compilation_options instead."
465                )
466            )
467        if circuit_compilation_options is None:
468            cc_options_kwargs = {}
469            if "max_circuit_duration_over_t2" in unknown_options:
470                cc_options_kwargs["max_circuit_duration_over_t2"] = unknown_options.pop(
471                    "max_circuit_duration_over_t2"
472                )
473            if "heralding_mode" in unknown_options:
474                cc_options_kwargs["heralding_mode"] = unknown_options.pop(
475                    "heralding_mode"
476                )
477            circuit_compilation_options = CircuitCompilationOptions(**cc_options_kwargs)
478
479        if unknown_options:
480            warnings.warn(f"Unknown backend option(s): {unknown_options}")
481
482        if circuit_callback:
483            circuit_callback(circuits)
484
485        circuits_serialized: CircuitBatch = [
486            self.serialize_circuit(circuit, qubit_index_to_name) for circuit in circuits
487        ]
488
489        if self._use_default_calibration_set:
490            default_calset_id = self.architecture.calibration_set_id
491            if self._calibration_set_id != default_calset_id:
492                warnings.warn(
493                    f"Server default calibration set has changed from {self._calibration_set_id} "
494                    f"to {default_calset_id}. Create a new IQMBackend if you wish to transpile the "
495                    "circuits using the new calibration set."
496                )
497        try:
498
499            def create_run_request(
500                circuits: CircuitBatch,
501                calibration_set_id: UUID | str,
502                *,
503                qubit_mapping: QubitMapping | None = None,
504                shots: int = 1,
505                options: CircuitCompilationOptions | None = None,
506            ) -> CircuitJobDefinition:
507                """Create a run request for executing circuits without sending it to the server.
508
509                This is called in :meth:`submit_circuits` and does not need to be called separately in normal usage.
510
511                Can be used to inspect the run request that would be submitted by :meth:`submit_circuits`, without actually
512                submitting it for execution.
513
514                Args:
515                    circuits: Circuits to be executed.
516                    qubit_mapping: Mapping of logical qubit names to physical qubit names.
517                        Can be set to ``None`` if all ``circuits`` already use physical qubit names.
518                        Note that the ``qubit_mapping`` is used for all ``circuits``.
519                    calibration_set_id: ID of the calibration set to use, or ``None`` to use the current default calibration.
520                    shots: Number of times ``circuits`` are executed. Must be greater than zero.
521                    options: Various discrete options for compiling quantum circuits to instruction schedules.
522
523                Returns:
524                    CircuitJobDefinition that would be submitted by equivalent call to :meth:`submit_circuits`.
525
526                """
527                if shots < 1:
528                    raise ValueError("Number of shots must be greater than zero.")
529                if options is None:
530                    options = CircuitCompilationOptions()
531
532                for i, circuit in enumerate(circuits):
533                    try:
534                        if isinstance(circuit, _Circuit):
535                            raise CircuitValidationError(
536                                f"Circuit {i}: obsolete circuit type."
537                            )
538                        if isinstance(circuit, QIRCode):
539                            # do not validate
540                            continue
541                        # validate the circuit against the static information in iqm.iqm_client.models._SUPPORTED_OPERATIONS
542                        validate_circuit(circuit)
543                    except ValueError as e:
544                        raise CircuitValidationError(
545                            f"The circuit at index {i} failed the validation: {e}"
546                        ).with_traceback(e.__traceback__)
547
548                dynamic_quantum_architecture = self.architecture
549
550                validate_qubit_mapping(
551                    dynamic_quantum_architecture, circuits, qubit_mapping
552                )
553                # validate the circuit against the calibration-dependent dynamic quantum architecture
554                validate_circuit_instructions(
555                    dynamic_quantum_architecture,
556                    circuits,
557                    qubit_mapping,
558                    validate_moves=options.move_gate_validation,
559                    must_close_sandwiches=False,
560                )
561
562                return CircuitJobDefinition(
563                    qubit_mapping=qubit_mapping,
564                    circuits=circuits,
565                    calibration_set_id=calibration_set_id
566                    if is_valid_uuid(calibration_set_id)
567                    else None,
568                    shots=shots,
569                    max_circuit_duration_over_t2=options.max_circuit_duration_over_t2,
570                    heralding_mode=options.heralding_mode,
571                    move_gate_validation=options.move_gate_validation,
572                    move_gate_frame_tracking=options.move_gate_frame_tracking,
573                    active_reset_cycles=options.active_reset_cycles,
574                    dd_mode=options.dd_mode,
575                    dd_strategy=options.dd_strategy,
576                )
577
578            # Local copy of IQMClient.create_run_request (35.x) / create_circuit_job_definition (36.x),
579            # validating against the cached architecture instead of calling the IQM server.
580            run_request = create_run_request(
581                circuits_serialized,
582                calibration_set_id=self._calibration_set_id,
583                shots=shots,
584                options=circuit_compilation_options,
585            )
586        except CircuitValidationError as e:
587            raise CircuitValidationError(
588                f"{e}\nMake sure the circuits have been transpiled using the same backend that you used to submit "
589                f"the circuits."
590            ) from e
591
592        return run_request
593
594    def run(
595        self,
596        run_input: QuantumCircuit | list[QuantumCircuit],
597        shots: int | None = None,
598        **options,
599    ):
600        """Submit circuit(s) for execution through HEAppE.
601
602        Args:
603            run_input: Transpiled circuit(s) to run.
604            shots: Shots per circuit; ``backend.options.shots`` if ``None``.
605            **options: ``memory``, ``job_name``, ``walltime_limit_secs``, ``use_sessions``,
606                ``circuit_compilation_options``, ``circuit_callback``, ``qubit_index_to_name``.
607
608        Returns:
609            QJob: The submitted job.
610        """
611        if shots is None:
612            shots = int(self.options.shots)
613        circuits = (
614            [run_input] if isinstance(run_input, QuantumCircuit) else list(run_input)
615        )
616
617        run_request = self.create_circuit_job_definition(
618            run_input=circuits,
619            shots=shots,
620            circuit_compilation_options=options.get(
621                "circuit_compilation_options", CircuitCompilationOptions()
622            ),
623            circuit_callback=options.get("circuit_callback"),
624            qubit_index_to_name=options.get("qubit_index_to_name"),
625        )
626
627        serialized_run_request = run_request.model_dump_json()
628
629        payloads = {"run_request": serialized_run_request}
630
631        circuit_headers = [
632            {"name": c.name, "metadata": dict(c.metadata or {})} for c in circuits
633        ]
634        return self._submit(
635            payloads, shots=shots, circuit_headers=circuit_headers, **options
636        )
637
638    def transpile(
639        self, circuits: list[QuantumCircuit] | QuantumCircuit, **kwargs
640    ) -> list[QuantumCircuit] | QuantumCircuit:
641        """Transpile the given circuits to the IQM backend's native gate set and qubit mapping.
642
643        Keeps each circuit's name and metadata, as ``qiskit.transpile`` does
644        (``transpile_to_IQM`` drops the metadata on backends with a resonator).
645        """
646        if isinstance(circuits, list):
647            return [self._transpile_one(circuit, **kwargs) for circuit in circuits]
648        return self._transpile_one(circuits, **kwargs)
649
650    def _transpile_one(self, circuit: QuantumCircuit, **kwargs) -> QuantumCircuit:
651        """Transpile one circuit and restore its name and metadata."""
652        transpiled = transpile_to_IQM(circuit=circuit, backend=self, **kwargs)
653        transpiled.name = circuit.name
654        transpiled.metadata = dict(circuit.metadata or {})
655        return transpiled

Works with every supported IQM stack. Stack-specific subclasses (QBackendIQM35, QBackendIQM36) set iqm_stack and override the hooks below where the IQM libraries differ.

239    def result_to_qiskit(
240        self,
241        raw: list[dict],
242        measurements_raw: list[dict] | None = None,
243        reg_name: str = "meas",
244    ) -> PrimitiveResult:
245        """
246        Convert raw results to a Qiskit PrimitiveResult object.
247
248        Args:
249            raw: A list of dictionaries containing measurement keys and counts.
250                 Each dictionary should have the form:
251                 {"measurement_keys": [...], "counts": {...}}
252            measurements_raw: Optional, one dictionary per PUB containing raw measurements.
253                              If provided, used instead of counts to preserve shot order.
254                              Format: {key: [[bit, ...], ...shots]}
255            reg_name: The name of the classical register to use for measurement results.
256
257        Bitstrings follow the Qiskit order (registers in circuit order, clbit 0
258        rightmost), using the IQM measurement keys. Results with other keys are
259        read as given, most significant bit first.
260
261        Returns:
262            A PrimitiveResult object containing the processed measurement results.
263        Raises:
264            ValueError: If the number of raw results does not match the number of measurement sets.
265            ValueError: If the shot counts differ between keys in a PUB.
266            ValueError: If the number of shots in measurements does not match the sum of counts.
267        """
268        if measurements_raw is not None and len(measurements_raw) != len(raw):
269            raise ValueError(
270                f"{len(raw)} results but {len(measurements_raw)} measurement sets"
271            )
272
273        pubs = []
274        for i, item in enumerate(raw):
275            keys = item["measurement_keys"]
276            item, m = _to_qiskit_order(
277                item, measurements_raw[i] if measurements_raw is not None else None
278            )
279            read_keys = item["measurement_keys"]
280
281            if m is not None:
282                cols = [
283                    np.asarray(m[k], dtype=bool).reshape(len(m[k]), -1)
284                    for k in read_keys
285                ]
286                if len({c.shape[0] for c in cols}) != 1:
287                    raise ValueError(f"PUB {i}: keys have different shot counts")
288                bitarray = BitArray.from_bool_array(
289                    np.concatenate(cols, axis=1), order="big"
290                )
291
292                if "counts" in item and bitarray.num_shots != sum(
293                    item["counts"].values()
294                ):
295                    raise ValueError(f"PUB {i}: shots in measurements != sum of counts")
296            else:
297                n = len(next(iter(item["counts"])))
298                int_counts = {int(bs, 2): c for bs, c in item["counts"].items()}
299                bitarray = BitArray.from_counts(int_counts, num_bits=n)
300
301            data = DataBin(**{reg_name: bitarray}, shape=bitarray.shape)
302            pubs.append(SamplerPubResult(data, metadata={"measurement_keys": keys}))
303        return PrimitiveResult(pubs, metadata={})

Convert raw results to a Qiskit PrimitiveResult object.

Each dictionary should have the form: {"measurement_keys": [...], "counts": {...}} measurements_raw: Optional, one dictionary per PUB containing raw measurements. If provided, used instead of counts to preserve shot order. Format: {key: [[bit, ...], ...shots]} reg_name: The name of the classical register to use for measurement results.

Bitstrings follow the Qiskit order (registers in circuit order, clbit 0 rightmost), using the IQM measurement keys. Results with other keys are read as given, most significant bit first.

Returns: A PrimitiveResult object containing the processed measurement results. Raises: ValueError: If the number of raw results does not match the number of measurement sets. ValueError: If the shot counts differ between keys in a PUB. ValueError: If the number of shots in measurements does not match the sum of counts.

def result_to_qiskit_legacy( self, raw: list[dict], measurements_raw: list[dict] | None = None, reg_name: str = 'meas', backend_name: str = 'my_backend', job_id: str = '', circuit_headers: list[dict[str, typing.Any]] | None = None) -> qiskit.result.result.Result: 
305    def result_to_qiskit_legacy(
306        self,
307        raw: list[dict],
308        measurements_raw: list[dict] | None = None,
309        reg_name: str = "meas",
310        backend_name: str = "my_backend",
311        job_id: str = "",
312        circuit_headers: list[dict[str, Any]] | None = None,
313    ) -> Result:
314        """
315        Convert raw results to a Qiskit Result object in legacy format.
316
317        Args:
318            raw: A list of dictionaries containing measurement keys and counts.
319                 Each dictionary should have the form:
320                 {"measurement_keys": [...], "counts": {...}}
321            measurements: Optional, one dictionary per PUB containing raw measurements.
322                          If provided, used instead of counts to preserve shot order.
323                          Format: {key: [[bit, ...], ...shots]}
324            reg_name: The name of the classical register to use for measurement results.
325            backend_name: The name of the backend used for the execution.
326            job_id: The ID of the job that produced the results.
327            circuit_headers: Optional, one ``{"name": ..., "metadata": ...}`` per circuit,
328                copied into each experiment's header (so ``get_counts(circuit)`` works).
329                Experiments are named ``circuit-<i>`` without it.
330
331        Bitstrings follow the Qiskit order (registers in circuit order, clbit 0
332        rightmost), using the IQM measurement keys. The IQM keys also give the
333        classical registers, so counts read e.g. ``"0 01"`` for registers ``a`` (2 bits)
334        and ``b`` (1 bit), as in Qiskit. Results with other keys are read as given,
335        most significant bit first, as one register ``reg_name``.
336
337        Returns:
338            A Result object containing the processed measurement results.
339
340        Raises:
341            ValueError: If the number of raw results does not match the number of measurement sets.
342        """
343
344        if circuit_headers is not None and len(circuit_headers) != len(raw):
345            circuit_headers = None  # e.g. a job re-created with different circuits
346
347        exps = []
348        for i, item in enumerate(raw):
349            keys = item["measurement_keys"]
350            creg_sizes = _iqm_creg_sizes(keys)
351            info = circuit_headers[i] if circuit_headers else {}
352            item, m = _to_qiskit_order(
353                item, measurements_raw[i] if measurements_raw is not None else None
354            )
355            counts = {hex(int(bs, 2)): c for bs, c in item["counts"].items()}
356            n = len(next(iter(item["counts"])))
357
358            memory = None
359            if m is not None:
360                per_key = [m[k] for k in item["measurement_keys"]]  # [key][shot][bit]
361                shots = len(per_key[0])
362                bitstrs = [
363                    "".join(str(int(b)) for k in per_key for b in k[s])
364                    for s in range(shots)
365                ]
366                memory = [hex(int(s, 2)) for s in bitstrs]
367
368            exps.append(
369                ExperimentResult(
370                    shots=sum(item["counts"].values()),
371                    success=True,
372                    data=ExperimentResultData(counts=counts, memory=memory),
373                    header={
374                        "name": info.get("name") or f"circuit-{i}",
375                        "creg_sizes": creg_sizes or [[reg_name, n]],
376                        "memory_slots": n,
377                        "metadata": info.get("metadata") or {},
378                        "measurement_keys": keys,
379                    },
380                )
381            )
382
383        return Result(
384            backend_name=backend_name,
385            backend_version="1.0",
386            job_id=job_id,
387            success=True,
388            results=exps,
389        )

Convert raw results to a Qiskit Result object in legacy format.

Args: raw: A list of dictionaries containing measurement keys and counts. Each dictionary should have the form: {"measurement_keys": [...], "counts": {...}} measurements: Optional, one dictionary per PUB containing raw measurements. If provided, used instead of counts to preserve shot order. Format: {key: [[bit, ...], ...shots]} reg_name: The name of the classical register to use for measurement results. backend_name: The name of the backend used for the execution. job_id: The ID of the job that produced the results. circuit_headers: Optional, one {"name": ..., "metadata": ...} per circuit, copied into each experiment's header (so get_counts(circuit) works). Experiments are named circuit-<i> without it.

Bitstrings follow the Qiskit order (registers in circuit order, clbit 0 rightmost), using the IQM measurement keys. The IQM keys also give the classical registers, so counts read e.g. "0 01" for registers a (2 bits) and b (1 bit), as in Qiskit. Results with other keys are read as given, most significant bit first, as one register reg_name.

Returns: A Result object containing the processed measurement results.

Raises: ValueError: If the number of raw results does not match the number of measurement sets.

Alias of create_circuit_job_definition() (iqm-client 35.x name).

def create_circuit_job_definition( self, run_input: qiskit.circuit.quantumcircuit.QuantumCircuit | list[qiskit.circuit.quantumcircuit.QuantumCircuit], shots: int = 1024, circuit_compilation_options: iqm.iqm_client.models.CircuitCompilationOptions | None = None, circuit_callback: Callable[[list[qiskit.circuit.quantumcircuit.QuantumCircuit]], typing.Any] | None = None, qubit_index_to_name: dict[int, str] | None = None, **unknown_options) -> iqm.station_control.interface.models.circuit.PostJobsRequest: 
410    def create_circuit_job_definition(
411        self,
412        run_input: QuantumCircuit | list[QuantumCircuit],
413        shots: int = 1024,
414        circuit_compilation_options: CircuitCompilationOptions | None = None,
415        circuit_callback: Callable[[list[QuantumCircuit]], Any] | None = None,
416        qubit_index_to_name: dict[int, str] | None = None,
417        **unknown_options,
418    ) -> CircuitJobDefinition:
419        """Create a circuit job definition (run request) without submitting it for execution.
420
421        This can be used to check what would be submitted for execution by an equivalent call to :meth:`run`.
422
423        Args:
424            run_input: Same as in :meth:`run`.
425
426        Args:
427            shots: Number of repetitions of each circuit, for sampling.
428            circuit_compilation_options:
429                Compilation options for the circuits, passed on to :class:`~iqm.iqm_client.iqm_client.IQMClient`.
430                If ``None``, the defaults of the :class:`~iqm.iqm_client.models.CircuitCompilationOptions`
431                class are used.
432            circuit_callback:
433                Callback function that, if provided, will be called for the circuits before sending
434                them to the device.  This may be useful in situations when you do not have explicit
435                control over transpilation, but need some information on how it was done. This can
436                happen, for example, when you use pre-implemented algorithms and experiments in
437                Qiskit, where the implementation of the said algorithm or experiment takes care of
438                delivering correctly transpiled circuits to the backend. This callback method gives
439                you a chance to look into those transpiled circuits, and extract any info you need.
440                As a side effect, you can also use this callback to modify the transpiled circuits
441                in-place, just before execution; however, we do not recommend to use it for this
442                purpose.
443            qubit_index_to_name: Mapping from qubit indices in the circuit to qubit names on the device.
444                If ``None``, :attr:`.IQMBackendBase.index_to_qubit_name` will be used.
445            unknown_options: Backwards compatibility for deprecated parameters.
446
447        Returns:
448            The created circuit job definition.
449
450        """
451        circuits = [run_input] if isinstance(run_input, QuantumCircuit) else run_input
452
453        if len(circuits) == 0:
454            raise ValueError("Empty list of circuits submitted for execution.")
455
456        # Catch old iqm-client options
457        if (
458            "max_circuit_duration_over_t2" in unknown_options
459            or "heralding_mode" in unknown_options
460        ):
461            warnings.warn(
462                DeprecationWarning(
463                    "max_circuit_duration_over_t2 and heralding_mode are deprecated, please use "
464                    + "circuit_compilation_options instead."
465                )
466            )
467        if circuit_compilation_options is None:
468            cc_options_kwargs = {}
469            if "max_circuit_duration_over_t2" in unknown_options:
470                cc_options_kwargs["max_circuit_duration_over_t2"] = unknown_options.pop(
471                    "max_circuit_duration_over_t2"
472                )
473            if "heralding_mode" in unknown_options:
474                cc_options_kwargs["heralding_mode"] = unknown_options.pop(
475                    "heralding_mode"
476                )
477            circuit_compilation_options = CircuitCompilationOptions(**cc_options_kwargs)
478
479        if unknown_options:
480            warnings.warn(f"Unknown backend option(s): {unknown_options}")
481
482        if circuit_callback:
483            circuit_callback(circuits)
484
485        circuits_serialized: CircuitBatch = [
486            self.serialize_circuit(circuit, qubit_index_to_name) for circuit in circuits
487        ]
488
489        if self._use_default_calibration_set:
490            default_calset_id = self.architecture.calibration_set_id
491            if self._calibration_set_id != default_calset_id:
492                warnings.warn(
493                    f"Server default calibration set has changed from {self._calibration_set_id} "
494                    f"to {default_calset_id}. Create a new IQMBackend if you wish to transpile the "
495                    "circuits using the new calibration set."
496                )
497        try:
498
499            def create_run_request(
500                circuits: CircuitBatch,
501                calibration_set_id: UUID | str,
502                *,
503                qubit_mapping: QubitMapping | None = None,
504                shots: int = 1,
505                options: CircuitCompilationOptions | None = None,
506            ) -> CircuitJobDefinition:
507                """Create a run request for executing circuits without sending it to the server.
508
509                This is called in :meth:`submit_circuits` and does not need to be called separately in normal usage.
510
511                Can be used to inspect the run request that would be submitted by :meth:`submit_circuits`, without actually
512                submitting it for execution.
513
514                Args:
515                    circuits: Circuits to be executed.
516                    qubit_mapping: Mapping of logical qubit names to physical qubit names.
517                        Can be set to ``None`` if all ``circuits`` already use physical qubit names.
518                        Note that the ``qubit_mapping`` is used for all ``circuits``.
519                    calibration_set_id: ID of the calibration set to use, or ``None`` to use the current default calibration.
520                    shots: Number of times ``circuits`` are executed. Must be greater than zero.
521                    options: Various discrete options for compiling quantum circuits to instruction schedules.
522
523                Returns:
524                    CircuitJobDefinition that would be submitted by equivalent call to :meth:`submit_circuits`.
525
526                """
527                if shots < 1:
528                    raise ValueError("Number of shots must be greater than zero.")
529                if options is None:
530                    options = CircuitCompilationOptions()
531
532                for i, circuit in enumerate(circuits):
533                    try:
534                        if isinstance(circuit, _Circuit):
535                            raise CircuitValidationError(
536                                f"Circuit {i}: obsolete circuit type."
537                            )
538                        if isinstance(circuit, QIRCode):
539                            # do not validate
540                            continue
541                        # validate the circuit against the static information in iqm.iqm_client.models._SUPPORTED_OPERATIONS
542                        validate_circuit(circuit)
543                    except ValueError as e:
544                        raise CircuitValidationError(
545                            f"The circuit at index {i} failed the validation: {e}"
546                        ).with_traceback(e.__traceback__)
547
548                dynamic_quantum_architecture = self.architecture
549
550                validate_qubit_mapping(
551                    dynamic_quantum_architecture, circuits, qubit_mapping
552                )
553                # validate the circuit against the calibration-dependent dynamic quantum architecture
554                validate_circuit_instructions(
555                    dynamic_quantum_architecture,
556                    circuits,
557                    qubit_mapping,
558                    validate_moves=options.move_gate_validation,
559                    must_close_sandwiches=False,
560                )
561
562                return CircuitJobDefinition(
563                    qubit_mapping=qubit_mapping,
564                    circuits=circuits,
565                    calibration_set_id=calibration_set_id
566                    if is_valid_uuid(calibration_set_id)
567                    else None,
568                    shots=shots,
569                    max_circuit_duration_over_t2=options.max_circuit_duration_over_t2,
570                    heralding_mode=options.heralding_mode,
571                    move_gate_validation=options.move_gate_validation,
572                    move_gate_frame_tracking=options.move_gate_frame_tracking,
573                    active_reset_cycles=options.active_reset_cycles,
574                    dd_mode=options.dd_mode,
575                    dd_strategy=options.dd_strategy,
576                )
577
578            # Local copy of IQMClient.create_run_request (35.x) / create_circuit_job_definition (36.x),
579            # validating against the cached architecture instead of calling the IQM server.
580            run_request = create_run_request(
581                circuits_serialized,
582                calibration_set_id=self._calibration_set_id,
583                shots=shots,
584                options=circuit_compilation_options,
585            )
586        except CircuitValidationError as e:
587            raise CircuitValidationError(
588                f"{e}\nMake sure the circuits have been transpiled using the same backend that you used to submit "
589                f"the circuits."
590            ) from e
591
592        return run_request

Create a circuit job definition (run request) without submitting it for execution.

This can be used to check what would be submitted for execution by an equivalent call to run().

Args: run_input: Same as in run().

Args: shots: Number of repetitions of each circuit, for sampling. circuit_compilation_options: Compilation options for the circuits, passed on to ~iqm.iqm_client.iqm_client.IQMClient. If None, the defaults of the ~iqm.iqm_client.models.CircuitCompilationOptions class are used. circuit_callback: Callback function that, if provided, will be called for the circuits before sending them to the device. This may be useful in situations when you do not have explicit control over transpilation, but need some information on how it was done. This can happen, for example, when you use pre-implemented algorithms and experiments in Qiskit, where the implementation of the said algorithm or experiment takes care of delivering correctly transpiled circuits to the backend. This callback method gives you a chance to look into those transpiled circuits, and extract any info you need. As a side effect, you can also use this callback to modify the transpiled circuits in-place, just before execution; however, we do not recommend to use it for this purpose. qubit_index_to_name: Mapping from qubit indices in the circuit to qubit names on the device. If None, .IQMBackendBase.index_to_qubit_name will be used. unknown_options: Backwards compatibility for deprecated parameters.

Returns: The created circuit job definition.

def run( self, run_input: qiskit.circuit.quantumcircuit.QuantumCircuit | list[qiskit.circuit.quantumcircuit.QuantumCircuit], shots: int | None = None, **options): 
594    def run(
595        self,
596        run_input: QuantumCircuit | list[QuantumCircuit],
597        shots: int | None = None,
598        **options,
599    ):
600        """Submit circuit(s) for execution through HEAppE.
601
602        Args:
603            run_input: Transpiled circuit(s) to run.
604            shots: Shots per circuit; ``backend.options.shots`` if ``None``.
605            **options: ``memory``, ``job_name``, ``walltime_limit_secs``, ``use_sessions``,
606                ``circuit_compilation_options``, ``circuit_callback``, ``qubit_index_to_name``.
607
608        Returns:
609            QJob: The submitted job.
610        """
611        if shots is None:
612            shots = int(self.options.shots)
613        circuits = (
614            [run_input] if isinstance(run_input, QuantumCircuit) else list(run_input)
615        )
616
617        run_request = self.create_circuit_job_definition(
618            run_input=circuits,
619            shots=shots,
620            circuit_compilation_options=options.get(
621                "circuit_compilation_options", CircuitCompilationOptions()
622            ),
623            circuit_callback=options.get("circuit_callback"),
624            qubit_index_to_name=options.get("qubit_index_to_name"),
625        )
626
627        serialized_run_request = run_request.model_dump_json()
628
629        payloads = {"run_request": serialized_run_request}
630
631        circuit_headers = [
632            {"name": c.name, "metadata": dict(c.metadata or {})} for c in circuits
633        ]
634        return self._submit(
635            payloads, shots=shots, circuit_headers=circuit_headers, **options
636        )

Submit circuit(s) for execution through HEAppE.

Args: run_input: Transpiled circuit(s) to run. shots: Shots per circuit; backend.options.shots if None. **options: memory, job_name, walltime_limit_secs, use_sessions, circuit_compilation_options, circuit_callback, qubit_index_to_name.

Returns: QJob: The submitted job.

def transpile( self, circuits: list[qiskit.circuit.quantumcircuit.QuantumCircuit] | qiskit.circuit.quantumcircuit.QuantumCircuit, **kwargs) -> list[qiskit.circuit.quantumcircuit.QuantumCircuit] | qiskit.circuit.quantumcircuit.QuantumCircuit: 
638    def transpile(
639        self, circuits: list[QuantumCircuit] | QuantumCircuit, **kwargs
640    ) -> list[QuantumCircuit] | QuantumCircuit:
641        """Transpile the given circuits to the IQM backend's native gate set and qubit mapping.
642
643        Keeps each circuit's name and metadata, as ``qiskit.transpile`` does
644        (``transpile_to_IQM`` drops the metadata on backends with a resonator).
645        """
646        if isinstance(circuits, list):
647            return [self._transpile_one(circuit, **kwargs) for circuit in circuits]

Transpile the given circuits to the IQM backend's native gate set and qubit mapping.

Keeps each circuit's name and metadata, as qiskit.transpile does (transpile_to_IQM drops the metadata on backends with a resonator).

class QBackendIQMFactory: 
 43class QBackendIQMFactory:
 44    """Create IQM backends that match both the installed IQM stack and the server.
 45
 46    Example::
 47
 48        backend = QBackendIQMFactory.create(client, backend_metadata)
 49        backend.iqm_stack  # IQMStack.IQM36
 50
 51    All methods are class methods; the class holds no state.
 52    """
 53
 54    @classmethod
 55    def installed_stack(cls) -> IQMStack:
 56        """Stack of the installed ``iqm-client`` (see :func:`.stack.installed_stack`)."""
 57        return installed_stack()
 58
 59    @classmethod
 60    def required_stack(cls, machine_info: QMachineInfo | None) -> IQMStack | None:
 61        """Recommended stack for the backend, or ``None`` if unknown (see :func:`.stack.required_stack`)."""
 62        return required_stack(machine_info)
 63
 64    @classmethod
 65    def resolve_stack(
 66        cls,
 67        machine_info: QMachineInfo | None,
 68        *,
 69        backend_name: str | None = None,
 70        strict: bool = True,
 71    ) -> IQMStack:
 72        """Pick the stack to use for a backend.
 73
 74        Args:
 75            machine_info: Parsed ``MachineInfo`` of the backend.
 76            backend_name: Used in messages only.
 77            strict: Raise if the installed stack does not work with the backend.
 78                If ``False``, log a warning and use the installed stack.
 79
 80        Returns:
 81            The installed stack (it is the only one that can be imported).
 82
 83        Raises:
 84            QException: No supported ``iqm-client`` installed, or (``strict``)
 85                the installed stack does not work with the backend.
 86        """
 87        installed = installed_stack()
 88        compatible = compatible_stacks(machine_info)
 89        name = backend_name or "<backend>"
 90        reported = machine_info.station_control_version if machine_info else None
 91
 92        if not compatible:
 93            log.warning(
 94                "Backend '%s' reports station_control_version=%r; cannot tell which IQM "
 95                "stack it needs. Using the installed one (%s).",
 96                name,
 97                reported,
 98                installed,
 99            )
100            return installed
101
102        if installed not in compatible:
103            required = compatible[0]
104            msg = (
105                f"Backend '{name}' runs IQM station-control {reported}, which needs the "
106                f"{required.value} IQM stack, but iqm-client {installed_iqm_client_version()} "
107                f"({installed.value}) is installed. Install the matching libraries with: "
108                f"{install_hint(required)}"
109            )
110            if strict:
111                raise QException(msg)
112            log.warning("%s. Continuing with %s (strict=False).", msg, installed.value)
113        return installed
114
115    @classmethod
116    def adapter(cls, stack: IQMStack | None = None) -> ModuleType:
117        """Import the adapter module of a stack.
118
119        Args:
120            stack: Stack to load; the installed one if ``None``.
121
122        Returns:
123            The ``qheappe_client.iqm_compat.iqm35`` / ``iqm36`` module.
124
125        Raises:
126            QException: The stack's libraries are not installed.
127        """
128        stack = stack or installed_stack()
129        try:
130            return importlib.import_module(f"{__package__}.{stack.value}")
131        except ImportError as e:
132            raise QException(
133                f"Cannot load the {stack.value} IQM stack ({e}). "
134                f"Install it with: {install_hint(stack)}"
135            ) from e
136
137    @classmethod
138    def backend_class(cls, stack: IQMStack | None = None) -> type[QBackendIQM]:
139        """Backend class of a stack (the installed one if ``None``)."""
140        stack = stack or installed_stack()
141        return getattr(cls.adapter(stack), _BACKEND_CLASS_NAME[stack])
142
143    @classmethod
144    def create(
145        cls,
146        client: QClient,
147        backend_metadata: QBackendMetadata,
148        calibration_set_id: UUID | str | None = None,
149        *,
150        use_metrics: bool = False,
151        strict: bool = True,
152        **kwargs: Any,
153    ) -> QBackendIQM:
154        """Build the IQM backend matching the installed stack and the server.
155
156        Args:
157            client: Client bound to the backend.
158            backend_metadata: Metadata with the dynamic architecture loaded.
159            calibration_set_id: Calibration set the architecture was fetched for.
160            use_metrics: Load calibration metrics into the transpiler target.
161            strict: See :meth:`resolve_stack`.
162            **kwargs: Passed to the backend constructor.
163
164        Returns:
165            A ``QBackendIQM35`` or ``QBackendIQM36`` instance.
166
167        Raises:
168            QException: See :meth:`resolve_stack` and :meth:`adapter`.
169            ValueError: The metadata has no dynamic architecture.
170        """
171        if backend_metadata.dynamic_architecture is None:
172            raise ValueError(
173                f"Backend '{backend_metadata.backend_name}' has no dynamic architecture."
174            )
175        stack = cls.resolve_stack(
176            backend_metadata.machine_info,
177            backend_name=backend_metadata.backend_name,
178            strict=strict,
179        )
180        backend_cls = cls.backend_class(stack)
181        return backend_cls(
182            client=client,
183            architecture=backend_metadata.dynamic_architecture,
184            use_metrics=use_metrics,
185            backend_metadata=backend_metadata,
186            calibration_set_id=calibration_set_id,
187            **kwargs,
188        )

Create IQM backends that match both the installed IQM stack and the server.

Example::

backend = QBackendIQMFactory.create(client, backend_metadata)
backend.iqm_stack  # IQMStack.IQM36

All methods are class methods; the class holds no state.

@classmethod
def resolve_stack( cls, machine_info: qheappe_client.backend_metadata.QMachineInfo | None, *, backend_name: str | None = None, strict: bool = True) -> IQMStack: 
 64    @classmethod
 65    def resolve_stack(
 66        cls,
 67        machine_info: QMachineInfo | None,
 68        *,
 69        backend_name: str | None = None,
 70        strict: bool = True,
 71    ) -> IQMStack:
 72        """Pick the stack to use for a backend.
 73
 74        Args:
 75            machine_info: Parsed ``MachineInfo`` of the backend.
 76            backend_name: Used in messages only.
 77            strict: Raise if the installed stack does not work with the backend.
 78                If ``False``, log a warning and use the installed stack.
 79
 80        Returns:
 81            The installed stack (it is the only one that can be imported).
 82
 83        Raises:
 84            QException: No supported ``iqm-client`` installed, or (``strict``)
 85                the installed stack does not work with the backend.
 86        """
 87        installed = installed_stack()
 88        compatible = compatible_stacks(machine_info)
 89        name = backend_name or "<backend>"
 90        reported = machine_info.station_control_version if machine_info else None
 91
 92        if not compatible:
 93            log.warning(
 94                "Backend '%s' reports station_control_version=%r; cannot tell which IQM "
 95                "stack it needs. Using the installed one (%s).",
 96                name,
 97                reported,
 98                installed,
 99            )
100            return installed
101
102        if installed not in compatible:
103            required = compatible[0]
104            msg = (
105                f"Backend '{name}' runs IQM station-control {reported}, which needs the "
106                f"{required.value} IQM stack, but iqm-client {installed_iqm_client_version()} "
107                f"({installed.value}) is installed. Install the matching libraries with: "
108                f"{install_hint(required)}"
109            )
110            if strict:
111                raise QException(msg)
112            log.warning("%s. Continuing with %s (strict=False).", msg, installed.value)
113        return installed

Pick the stack to use for a backend.

Args: machine_info: Parsed MachineInfo of the backend. backend_name: Used in messages only. strict: Raise if the installed stack does not work with the backend. If False, log a warning and use the installed stack.

Returns: The installed stack (it is the only one that can be imported).

Raises: QException: No supported iqm-client installed, or (strict) the installed stack does not work with the backend.

@classmethod
def adapter( cls, stack: IQMStack | None = None) -> module: 
115    @classmethod
116    def adapter(cls, stack: IQMStack | None = None) -> ModuleType:
117        """Import the adapter module of a stack.
118
119        Args:
120            stack: Stack to load; the installed one if ``None``.
121
122        Returns:
123            The ``qheappe_client.iqm_compat.iqm35`` / ``iqm36`` module.
124
125        Raises:
126            QException: The stack's libraries are not installed.
127        """
128        stack = stack or installed_stack()
129        try:
130            return importlib.import_module(f"{__package__}.{stack.value}")
131        except ImportError as e:
132            raise QException(
133                f"Cannot load the {stack.value} IQM stack ({e}). "
134                f"Install it with: {install_hint(stack)}"
135            ) from e
